inspected_by: assistant (Phase 3.8 visual inspection of the 16 sprites extracted from the black-background sheet, on white at 1-2x zoom); this is not a person's review

conventions.sprite_axes: x = image right, y = image down, z = toward the viewer (front camera)
conventions.palm_normal_sprite: unit vector out of the palm surface, in the sprite as drawn
conventions.angles: degrees from sprite-down, + toward image left (the rig's 'ang' convention)
conventions.handedness_rule: with fingers f and palm normal n (sprite axes), a right hand has its thumb along f x n, a left hand along n x f
conventions.rotation_tolerance_deg: how far the drawing may be turned in the image plane from how it was drawn before its reading changes (a cup tips, a thumb stops pointing up, relaxed fingers stop hanging). A camera-facing flat hand keeps its palm reading at any angle, so its tolerance is 180

geometry_note: the 16 drawings have the same outlines as the schoolboy sleeve-free sheet (silhouette IoU 0.979-0.989 per cell, measured), recoloured with peach skin and two-tone cel shading on a black background; the reading below was made on this sheet and agrees with the Phase 3.7 reading of those outlines

r1c1.cues: re-inspected in Phase 3.8.1: the fingers hang straight and together and the thumb is a short digit at the image-right edge, partly behind the hand outline; no palm-side cue is drawn (the palm drawings of the same sheet, e.g. the open palms and cupped hands, show palm creases). Read as the BACK of a right hand. The Phase 3.7 palm reading as a left hand put the palm toward the camera with the thumb outward on a hanging arm (a fully supinated forearm), which is not a resting hand; the artist's own arms-down front view (references/schoolboy/character_sheet.jpg) shows hanging hands from the back with the thumbs toward the body. Assistant's reading, not a person's review; correct it in the Hand Inspector if the palm reading was intended
r1c1.gesture_semantics: a relaxed hanging hand: the fingers read as hanging under gravity only within about 50 deg of hanging

r1c2.cues: two palm creases, thumb to the image right, fingers down: the palm of a left hand faces the viewer
r1c2.gesture_semantics: open hand, palm toward the camera, fingers spread

r1c3.cues: the fronts of the curled fingers face the viewer, the thumb crosses them from the image right, wrist at the top: left hand
r1c3.gesture_semantics: closed fist seen from the finger side

r1c4.cues: index points image-left from a closed wrist on the image right, thumb on top, curled finger fronts toward the viewer: f = -x, n = +z, f x n = +y (up) -> RIGHT hand, although it sits in the left row group (same finding as the schoolboy sheet)
r1c4.gesture_semantics: index extended, other fingers curled; aimed by the wrist

r2c1.cues: wrist on the image left, curled fingers point image-right with their fronts to the viewer, thumb up: f = +x, n = +z, n x f = +y -> left hand
r2c1.gesture_semantics: thumbs-up: reads only while the thumb points up

r2c2.cues: C-shaped grip in profile, opening to the image right, wrist on the image left; a profile of a left hand and a mirrored right hand look the same, so handedness follows the row group and the outward wrist side (low confidence)
r2c2.gesture_semantics: grip around an object in front of the fingers (contact gesture)

r2c3.cues: back of the hand seen from above (no creases, knuckle shading), fingers down-right, thumb to the image left: n = (0, +0.74, -0.67), n x f has a -x component -> left hand
r2c3.gesture_semantics: flat hand resting palm-down on a surface below eye level

r2c4.cues: palm up, seen from the front and slightly above (palm creases visible), fingers to the image left curling up, the big rounded shape on top is the thumb on the far side, wrist on the image right: f = -x, n = up, f x n points away from the viewer -> thumb behind -> RIGHT hand, although it sits in the left row group
r2c4.gesture_semantics: cupped/offering palm-up hand; turned more than about 35 deg the cup tips, turned 180 deg it is palm-down

r3c1.cues: re-inspected in Phase 3.8.1: the fingers hang straight and together and the thumb is a short digit at the image-left edge, partly behind the hand outline; no palm-side cue is drawn (the palm drawings of the same sheet, e.g. the open palms and cupped hands, show palm creases). Read as the BACK of a left hand. The Phase 3.7 palm reading as a right hand put the palm toward the camera with the thumb outward on a hanging arm (a fully supinated forearm), which is not a resting hand; the artist's own arms-down front view (references/schoolboy/character_sheet.jpg) shows hanging hands from the back with the thumbs toward the body.
